issues.what: camera angle, field of view, horizon orientation, and sun position jump abruptly: the large yellow sun at the right edge in 722 shrinks into a small ball at upper right over black sky in 730, then leaps to upper-left-center as a white diffraction starburst in 739 while the vertical right limb flips to a diagonal horizon
issues.fix: drive the entire dive from one continuous 3D camera path and unified sun light source so the limb angle and solar position travel smoothly into the terrain entry frame

issues.what: camera motion reverses direction across the cover via a visible cross-dissolve: frames 985-992 push forward and downward over the terrain, then frames 993-996 pull rapidly backward from a brighter globe while the foreground crater dissolves out, the sun slides rightward, a dark ghost band appears above the right limb, and an orange nebula pops into the upper-left sky
issues.fix: decelerate forward terrain motion and pull upward and backward before the cover so velocity direction, horizon curvature, surface brightness, sun position, and background sky match the outgoing 3D globe seamlessly

issues.where: frames 1000-1034, sun, globe, and left sky
issues.what: between frames 1000 and 1007 the small white starburst sun pops into a huge yellow solar disc at the right edge while the pale gray globe shifts to warm brown shading and a bright orange dust cloud appears on the left, failing to match the blue-black sky and lower-left orbiting body from the opening hold in sheet-01.png
issues.fix: use a consistent solar scale, planet shader, and background starfield across hold, dive, and rise so the flight returns seamlessly to the same space environment it left

issues.where: frames 739-744, horizon, sun, and cratered surface
issues.what: the dive-to-terrain cover shows a multi-frame double exposure where a dark curved ghost band lingers in the upper-right sky above the incoming terrain horizon, the sun slides leftward while changing flare shape, and two misaligned crater fields dissolve through one another
issues.fix: register the outgoing globe horizon, crater coordinates, skybox, and solar flare position to the terrain camera at the handoff so the cover reads as one unbroken camera move

issues.where: frames 698-714, upper-left sky, lower-left body, and terminator
issues.what: entering the dive swaps visibly from the hold plate to a different 3D globe setup: between frames 698 and 706 the upper-left starfield drops to solid black, the bright orbiting dot at lower left vanishes, and sharper procedural bump craters pop in along the terminator
issues.fix: render the hold and dive from the same 3D globe, starfield, and scene elements so lighting, surface relief, and background stars carry across without a rig swap

issues.where: frames 739-742, high-contrast crater rims on right side
issues.what: fast radial motion breaks into discrete, comb-like stepped ghost copies along bright crater edges rather than a smooth continuous motion blur (also visible in sheet-06.png frames 988-994)
issues.fix: increase shutter sub-frame sampling or apply continuous motion-vector blur during peak dive and rise speeds so edges streak smoothly without multi-copy stepping

issues.where: frames 845-959, bright radial crater at mid-left
issues.what: bright white ejecta rays on the mid-left crater extrude upward into sharp vertical spikes as parallax increases (continuing into sheet-05.png frames 960-987) because bright albedo streaks are displaced as tall terrain height
issues.fix: decouple high-albedo ejecta rays from the elevation displacement map so surface ray markings remain flat on the terrain instead of stretching into needles
